full_judgment:
2. The present respondent Nos. 1-6 as plaintiffs instituted the Title Suit No. 132 of 1990 before the Court of Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for permanent injunction in respect of 0.17-3/4 acres of land appertaining to CS and. SA Plot No. 367 under CS Khatian No. 136 corresponding to SA Khatian No. 211 and Mutation Khatian No. 211/4 of Mouja Barua. The suit on transfer to the Court of Additional Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka was renumbered as Title Suit No. 98 of, 1992 which was again transferred to the Court of Assistant Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No. 137 of 1996. 

 3. The respondent Nos.1-6 as plaintiffs filed the aforesaid suit stating, inter alia, that Omar Ali Sarker was the original owner of the suit land and out of the suit land Abbas Ali Sarker, the son of said Omar Ali Sarker, was the owner and possessor of 7 annas share and Sadar Bewa, wife of Omar Ali, was owner to the extent of 2 arenas share and their names were correctly recorded in the CS Khatian; that Sadar Bewa died leaving one son named Abbas Ali and he became owner of 2 annas share of his mother and in this way, the said Abbas Ali became the owner of 9 annas share in the suit plots and since then he has been possessing the same for more than 12 years; that the said Abbas Ali died leaving behind 2 sons, namely, Asar Ali and Ayub Ali and one wife, Asia Khatun and subsequently said Asia died leaving behind aforesaid 2 sons and they got the land on the basis of amicable partition between the 2 brothers; that when Asgar Ali was in possession and enjoyment of his share in the suit land by cultivating the same and on payment of rent thereof, he transferred 0.16 acres of land out of the land described in schedule of the plaint to Abdus Sattar, predecessor of the plaintiff by a registered deed of sale dated 21-1-1948 and handed over possession to him and thereafter the plaintiff Nos.1 and 6 purchased 0.01-3/4 acres of land from Ayub Ali by a registered deed dated 30-1-1985 and got possession therein; that while father of the plaintiff was in possession and enjoyment of 0.06 acres of land by cultivating various crops thereon, SA and DP Khatians were prepared in his name and thereafter he died leaving behind 2 sons (plaintiff Nos. 2 and 30) and 3 daughters (plaintiff Nos. 1, 4 and 5) and they are in possession and enjoyment of the said land on payment of rent, taxes and mutating their names; that though the defendants have got no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land but on 27-5-1989 the defendants came to take away the crops forcibly but due to intervention they could not succeed in doing the same and in pursuance to that activities of the defendants, the plaintiff No. 1 made GD entry No. 1410 dated 27-5-1989 with the local police station and on investigation the local police found the plaintiff in possession of the suit land; that recently the defendants at the strength of an ineffective deed tried to dispossess the plaintiff forcibly from the suit land but due to timely intervention of the plaintiff and their relatives they could not succeed in doing so but threatened to dispossess them, so the suit. 

 4. The present petitioner as defendant No. 2 contested the suit by filing the joint written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint stating, inter alia, that Omar Ali was the original owner and possessor of the suit land and before CS operation said Omar Ali died leaving behind one wife, Sadar Bewa, 2 sons, named Abbas Ali and Meher Ali and 3 daughters, named Arjan, Samiron and Kadbanu and they inherited the said land according to their shares; that Meher Ali died before CS operation leaving behind only one son Dukkhu Miah; that since the aforesaid 3 daughters were living in the home of their respective husbands CS Khatian has been prepared in the name of Abbas Ali, Dukhu Mia, son of Meher Ali and Sadar Bewa and since then said Dukhu has been enjoying and possessing 0.16 acre of land to the North Eastern side of the suit plot and 0.23 acre to the Southern side and Abbas was in possession and enjoyment of 0.23 of land in the middle of the suit plot on amicable partition and thereafter said Sadar Bewa died leaving Abbas Ali and 3 daughters; that while said Abbas Ali was in possession and enjoyment of the said land, he died leaving one wife, Asia Khatun and 2 sons named Ayub Ali and Asgar Ali and 3 daughters named, Rosia, Monowara and Mukta and on amicable partition Asgar Ali got half from the Western side and half from the Western side and Ayub Ali got half from the Eastern side; that after the death of Abbas Ali his two sons namely, Asgar Ali and Ayub Ali inherited their share from the land left by his father and thereafter Asgar Ali transferred 0.16 acre of land out of said 0.23 acre of land to Abdus Sattar (predecessor of the plaintiff Nos.1-5) by a registered deed of sale dated 21-1-1948 on condition to recovery the same and accordingly on the same date i.e. on 21-1-1948 said Asgar Ali executed and registered a sale deed in favour of Abdus Sattar Raj but Asgar Ali did not handover the said land to Abdus Sattar Raj who had never enjoyed the said land; that 3 months after on 21-1-1948 Asgar Ali returned the said consideration money to Abdus Sattar in presence of Kelajuddin, Belal Uddin, Shahaj Uddin and others and told him to execute and register a deed in favour of him but he did not do so; that subsequently said Asgar Ali transferred the said land to defendant No. 1 by registered deed of sale dated 2-10-1948 and handed over possession to him and since then he has been possessing his own purchased land; that while he was in possession and enjoyment of the said land he transferred 0.0165 acres of land to the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 6 by a registered deed of sale dated 30-1-1985 and handed over possession to them; that the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 5 had never enjoyed and possessed the suit land rather since 2-10-1948 the defendant No. 1 has been possessing the suit land by cultivating various crops; that in the year 1988 the plaintiffs forcibly destroyed the crops cultivated by the defendant in their land and after the said occurrence the defendants filed a petition of complaint being No. 289A 1 of 1988 before the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and in the said case the learned Magistrate by his judgment and order dated 25-5-1989 convicted the plaintiffs and the learned Magistrate also found the defendants are in exclusive possession in the suit land and on the other hand, the plaintiffs have got no right and possession in the suit land and, as such, the suit of the plaintiffs is not maintainable in its present form, therefore, the same is liable to be dismissed with cost.
